## Operational Environment

### Systems Engineering View

This systems engineering view shows how Zulip operates, while looking at a larger company environment. I have added critical components to show how each supports one another and ultimately they all interact as well. We have main systems elements like; Zulip Application/Server, PostgreSQL database, and File/Attachment Storage.Then we look at the outer circles that show the systems enabled from system elements, also identifying where security threats are/how each could affect the system as a whole.

![][image1]

### Perceived Threats

1. Credential theft, giving access whether it's intentional or accidental can expose sensitive data to designed or intended users (by pertaining login information)

2. Phishing, usually links in a form of email that seems like it was sent by Zulip to compromise users as a different access point. 

3. Unauthorized access, when someone gets access to files or any sort of data that they are not supposed to. 

4. Software issues, attackers figure out weakness and exploit Zulip/components.

5. Insider threats, as someone who works or knows information, can expose a company's plans or information not intended for outside knowledge.

6. Account issues, an attacker could impersonate employees and gain access to confidential information or conversations. 

## Security Features 

Zulip states that it is GDPR and CCPA compliant which would be beneficial to us if we were an organization in the EU or California but it is still good to note and be aware of. For example, if we were an organization in the EU, we could allow users to edit their profile information, configure privacy settings, and delete their own messages and uploaded files. Organization admins could also edit any user’s profile information or deactivate accounts. We could export all data related to a Zulip user or organization. And the Zulip REST API would allow us to automate our processes for handling GDPR requests. ([https://zulip.com/help/gdpr-compliance](https://zulip.com/help/gdpr-compliance))

All Zulip clients require TLS encryption and authentication over HTTPS for data transmission to and from the server, both on LAN and the Internet.

End-to-end encryption ensures that message content and metadata are not visible to Apple, Google, or Zulip’s Mobile Push Notification Service.

Zulip can be self-hosted to further protect data and has support for encryption in transit and at rest. This gives us the opportunity to encrypt our database, uploads, and backups at rest on our own infrastructure. Because it can be self-hosted, their documentation says it can be hosted entirely behind our firewall, or on an air-gapped network.

Zulip also boasts about it custom security policies allowing us to set our own password strength requirements, revoke or reset any user’s credentials, set caps on session lengths and how long before the idle timeout kicks in, configurable log rotation policies, and we can set our own rate limits for API endpoints and authentication attempts.

## Team Motivation

Our team selected Zulip because we wanted to analyze an open-source project where data privacy and user confidentiality are critical. In the modern workplace, collaboration software serves as the central hub for sensitive corporate data, making it a prime target for security breaches. We were motivated to explore how a modern open-source platform balances seamless user collaboration with robust data protection. Specifically, we wanted to investigate the security engineering required to handle multi-tenant hosting safely, ensuring the data belonging to different organizations remains entirely isolated.This project offers us an opportunity to examine real-world security features and threat mitigation within an actively maintained open-source codebase.

## Open-Source Project Description

**What it is:** Zulip is an open-source team collaboration and chat application designed as a team collaboration tool. Zulip features a unique threading model, in which each message also has a topic, along with the content. Users can also organize conversations by subject within channels, aiming to improve productivity.

**Contributors and activity:** Zulip has a large and active contributor base. As of Zulip’s last update on OpenHub in June 2026, more than 160 contributors merged over 6000 commits year over year. Since the project's inception, over 6,000 people have contributed more than 145,000 commits to the project. In 2026, the **Zulip Foundation**, was founded to independently manage the project.

**Use and popularity:** Fortune 500 companies, leading open source projects, and thousands of other organizations use Zulip daily. On GitHub, the main repository has 25.9k stars.

**Languages and platform:** 55% of the code in Zulip is written in Python, while C++ and JavaScript make up 12% and 11% of the code, respectively. As for platforms supported, Zulip has mobile apps for iOS and Android, desktop clients for Windows, MacOS, and Linux, and terminal clients for Linux, macOS, and Windows.

**Documentation:** There are over 100 feature articles and guides in the Zulip help center. They have articles for both end-users and system administrators. Documentation can be found here: [https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/)

### Contribution Process

We must comply with the terms and conditions of the Zulip License without any additional terms or conditions.

AI is allowed so long as we understand and can explain the change we are proposing to make.

As far as the contribution process goes, on their [page](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/contributing/contributing.html), they have these steps:

1. Pick an issue to work on \- some issues are marked with “help wanted”  
2. Claim an issue  
   1. Post a comment in either the zulip/zulip or the zulip/zulip-terminal repositories with a comment that says “@zulipbot claim” to the issue thread and the GitHub workflow bot (Zulipbot) will assign the issue to you if it is not already being worked on.  
3. Follow best practices  
4. Submit a pull request \- [link](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/contributing/reviewable-prs.html)  
   1. Write your code with clarity in mind  
   2. Organize proposed changes into a series of commits that tell how the codebase will change  
   3. Explain the changes  
   4. Review your work  
   5. Submit the pull request for review

## Security-Related History

**Known Vulnerabilities:** Zulip supports hosting multiple organizations, known internally as realms, on a single server. Each organization should only operate within its own boundary. However, this boundary has failed more than once. In 2017, CVE-2017-0910 let an unauthorized user from one realm use the invitation system to create an account on any other realm on the same server.  It was fixed in Zulip Server 1.7.1. A similar flaw appeared in CVE-2022-21706, where users could join realms they were not invited to by accessing a reusable invitation link. This bypassed security restrictions for email domains and invitation only registration. There were also cases of users being granted elevated privileges.  

The most serious case of these was CVE-2025-31478, an authentication backend configuration bypass. Organizations can secure account creation by requiring successful sign in through Single Sign On (SSO) integration. This flaw allowed users to create an account without authenticating through the SSO provider. It was fixed in version 10.2.

CVE-2026-25742 was a missing authorization flaw. Even after the organization removed web public access, attachments from the public channels could still be downloaded by anyone without logging in. This issue was resolved in version 11.6

Zulip fixed more issues in the 12.2 release on August 10, 2026\. CVE IDs have been requested for these issues and are still waiting for assignment. Three of the issues were permission check failures that exposed data to users who were not authorized to view it. Guests could receive messages for channels they were not in by registering an event queue. Guests could also see profile data from any user in the organization by creating a draft message. The last two came from an OpenID connect backend that ignored the email\_verfied claim, which caused users to be logged into the wrong account, and it ignored the content length check increasing resource consumption.

More CVEs and security releases can be found [here](https://blog.zulip.com/tag/release-announcements/).

**Security-Related Engineering Decisions:** Zulip’s security model is designed to provide data protection by default. The processes behind it are well documented and easy to digest. The application is also flexible enough so that organizations can configure it to meet their own needs.

Data is protected in transit at every layer. All clients require TLS encryption and authentication over HTTPS when sending data to and from the server. As of Zulip Server 12.0, mobile push notifications are encrypted end-to-end between the server and device. This makes message content and metadata invisible to Apple’s or Google’s push infrastructure. Third party connections transmit data over same encrypted transport, and administrators can browse, manage and deactivate them as needed. All access to user data is routed through audited core libraries that consistently validate access controls.

The codebase is open source, so security teams and independent practitioners can audit the system for security issues themselves. The server ships with an extensive automated test suite that includes full coverage testing for security sensitive code paths. Zulip uses static type checking and automated code scanning to catch several common categories of security bugs before they enter the codebase. They have a very thorough code review process that verifies all changes. It can also be hosted behind a firewall or on an air-gapped network.

Security issues are reported to security@zulip.com or through their HackerOne disclosure program. A CVE ID is requested for confirmed issues. Once an issue is remediated, the fix is published to the main branch and current release branch.
